5.2.cite: He, Q., Huang, X., Liu, Y., Li, X., Huang, L., Park, I. H., et al. (2026). Multimedia-assisted narrative intervention for existential distress among patients with advanced cancer: a one-group pre–post study. Frontiers in Public Health, 14, 1932219.
5.2.uses: The authors compared scores before and after a 4-week intervention with paired-samples t-tests and reported each mean difference with its 95% confidence interval (for example, meaning in life rose by 0.42, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.51).

5.3.cite: García-Gil, A., Hernández-Jurado, B. I., Luna-Ruiz-Esparza, M. A., Espinoza-Angulo, E., Machado-Jiménez, H., Gómez-Campaña, H., et al. (2025). Prevalence and age-related trends of refractive errors in Mexican outpatients: a cross-sectional study. Frontiers in Public Health, 13, 1675138.
5.3.uses: The authors report prevalence proportions with exact 95% confidence intervals computed by the Clopper-Pearson method, which they chose for its accuracy in estimating intervals for proportions.

6.1.cite: Huang, M., Li, Z., Zheng, Y., & Yang, C. (2025). Cognitive processing of Chinese verbal irony: the role of reverse adjacency relations in reaction time and accuracy. Frontiers in Psychology, 16, 1619358.
6.1.uses: Before running paired t-tests on comprehension accuracy, the authors state a null hypothesis (no difference in mean accuracy between the two sentence groups) and an alternative hypothesis (the means are not equal), then judge the test against 0.05.

6.2.cite: Li, S., Huang, Y., Xu, C., Wu, J., & Qu, C. (2024). Asymmetric adaption in social learning: Understanding the dilemma of competition and cooperation. Behavioral Sciences, 14(8), 721.
6.2.uses: The authors set the significance level at p < 0.05 with a Bonferroni correction and also report Bayes factors that weigh the alternative hypothesis against the null, which shows p-values used with a stated alpha and supplemented by another measure of evidence.

6.3.cite: McGaffick, C., Gulrajani, N., Kong, N., & Adams, N. (2023). Learning in a crisis moment: a randomized controlled trial in emergency bystander intervention. BMC Psychology, 11(1), 212.
6.3.uses: The authors ran an a priori power analysis from pilot data (alpha 0.05, power 0.80, effect size 0.73), found that 60 participants were needed, and recruited about 150 for safety. They state a null and an alternative hypothesis for the trial.

6.4.cite: Šulejová, K., Líška, D., Liptáková, E., Szántová, M., Patarák, M., Koller, T., et al. (2022). Relationship between alcohol consumption and adverse childhood experiences in college students–A cross-sectional study. Frontiers in Psychology, 13, 1004651.
6.4.uses: A two-proportion z-test, pooled for H0: p1 = p2, was used to test whether the proportions of adverse childhood experiences were equal between men and women.

6.5.cite: Zou, L., Wu, J., & Liu, C. (2025). No detectable effects of chronic stress on moral decision-making are found: A data reanalysis and a pre-registered replication and extension. Behavioral Sciences, 15(8), 1068.
6.5.uses: The authors used a one-sample t-test to compare participants' mean probability of accepting a harmful action with a test value of 0.5, and found it was higher (t = 7.56, df = 207, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.52).

6.6.cite: D’Agostino, S. R., Landon, T. J., Roylance, A., Briggs, A., & Bhana-Lopez, N. (2025). Exploring the social validity and diffusion potential of common naturalistic developmental behavioral intervention strategies implemented in community preschools. Behavioral Sciences, 15(3), 357.
6.6.uses: Parents and autistic adults were compared with independent samples t-tests. Where group sizes were unequal and the homogeneity of variance assumption was not met, the authors switched to Welch's t-test (for example t = 3.3, df = 58.8) and reported Cohen's d.

6.7.cite: Liu, J., Liu, X., & Ding, M. (2024). The impact of a positive discipline group intervention on parenting self-efficacy among mothers of young children. Frontiers in Public Health, 12, 1461435.
6.7.uses: The authors used paired samples t-tests to compare mothers' parenting self-efficacy scores before and after a 6-week intervention, and independent samples t-tests to compare the intervention and control groups, with Cohen's d for the size of change.

6.8.cite: Huang, M., Li, Z., Zheng, Y., & Yang, C. (2025). Cognitive processing of Chinese verbal irony: the role of reverse adjacency relations in reaction time and accuracy. Frontiers in Psychology, 16, 1619358.
6.8.uses: After a significant paired t-test, the authors report Cohen's d = 0.455 with a 95% confidence interval and read it against the 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 benchmarks as a medium effect, saying the difference was significant but moderate in size.

6.9.cite: Puteikis, K., Ažukaitis, K., Dadurkevičienė, D., Simanauskas, K., Šileikienė, V., Jankauskienė, A., et al. (2024). Primary arterial hypertension associated with cognitive dysfunction in young adults: Results from a cross-sectional controlled study. Behavioral Sciences, 14(4), 321.
6.9.uses: The authors checked each continuous variable with the Shapiro-Wilk test, then compared the hypertension and control groups with Student's t-test when the data were normal and the Mann-Whitney U test when they were not.
